body: there'a an alternative way of coding this where we check length squared

Isn't this a behavior change from the old condition? The old threshold was relative to the angle, this one is relative to the cosine of the angle scaled up to fit in an angle range. It would change the effective value of threshold slightly. Perhaps too small of a difference to practically matter, but noting it anyways.

Oh, I had the wrong range to begin with (it should be `* 0.5 * Math::PI`). However, there should still be a slight difference between "atan with cross" and "simple dot" results, so if this is a problem as I commented in the description, perhaps the original formula should be used.

At any rate, I reverted it back considering that this is a place where accuracy should be prioritized over performance so much; Simple dot result is probably unsuitable if we are looking at anything other than 0/90/180 degrees, since atan is to correct the s-curve error in dot. Thanks.
Do we need to normalize basis here?
No, since src_dir and prof_dir are normalized.
